Supersedes the North-West-only version effective 1 January 2025. Applicability extended to all regions
following a successful pilot.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how a key holder is nominated and contacted outside of normal hours. It now
applies to every site in every region, extending the arrangement previously piloted in the North West
Region alone.

Policy statement

Each site, in every region, nominates 2 key holders who may be called by the alarm monitoring company
outside of hours — extending the arrangement piloted in the North West Region to Midlands and South
West — providing a reliable way of responding to an out-of-hours alarm activation without every incident
requiring the registered manager personally.

Definitions

**Key holder** a nominated staff member who can attend site out of hours if the alarm monitoring company
calls. **Alarm monitoring company** the external company monitoring the site's alarm system and calling a
key holder when it activates outside of hours. **Rollout** this version's extension of the previously North
West-only arrangement to every region.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager** nominates 2 key holders for their site, now including Midlands and South West
sites for the first time, and keeps the alarm monitoring company's contact list current. **A nominated key
holder** attends site promptly if called, assessing the alarm activation and taking appropriate action.
**Facilities** reviews the now-national arrangement's outcomes as part of ongoing monitoring.

first time.

activation.

3. Assess the cause of the activation on arrival, resetting the alarm if it is a false activation or escalating

Fire Evacuation Procedure — Riverside House

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how staff at Riverside House respond to a fire alarm and evacuate the building. It applies to every member of staff on shift, and is shared with every resident and visitor as appropriate to their understanding.

Policy statement

Riverside House uses a staged evacuation approach appropriate to a care setting where many residents have limited mobility, moving residents in immediate danger first while others are supported in a safe waiting area, rather than attempting a single simultaneous evacuation of the whole building.

Definitions

**PEEP** a Personal Emergency Evacuation Plan, prepared for every resident, setting out exactly how they are assisted to evacuate given their specific mobility and cognitive needs. **Fire warden** a trained staff member responsible for a specific zone during an evacuation. **Assembly point** the designated safe location outside the building where evacuated residents and staff gather.

Roles and responsibilities

**The fire warden on shift** directs the evacuation of their assigned zone according to each resident's PEEP. **The shift lead** calls the fire brigade, confirms the building is being evacuated, and accounts for every resident and staff member at the assembly point. **All staff** know the location of their nearest fire exit and evacuation equipment at all times.

On hearing the fire alarm, the fire warden for each zone begins evacuating residents according to their individual PEEP, prioritising anyone in immediate danger from the fire's location.

Call the fire brigade immediately; this is never delayed to first confirm whether the alarm is a false alert.

Use the evacuation chair for a resident whose PEEP requires it, only after staff have received evacuation chair training.

Move to the assembly point and complete a headcount against the day's resident and staff list, reporting any person unaccounted for to the fire brigade on arrival.

Asbestos Management Procedure

*Supersedes the version effective 1 January 2025. Oakfield Lodge added to scope following a newly confirmed asbestos survey; Harbour View, Meadow Court and Willow Bank remain out of scope as newer buildings.*

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group manages a confirmed asbestos register at a site where one applies. It now applies to Riverside House, Moorland View and Oakfield Lodge, following a newly confirmed asbestos survey at Oakfield Lodge; Harbour View, Meadow Court and Willow Bank remain out of scope as newer buildings.

Policy statement

Riverside House, Moorland View and now Oakfield Lodge each maintain an asbestos register; any work disturbing a fabric surface must check the register first, preventing accidental disturbance of a material that presents a serious health risk if damaged.

Definitions

**Asbestos register** the documented record of confirmed or presumed asbestos-containing material within a building, based on a professional survey. **Fabric surface** a wall, ceiling, floor or other building surface that may conceal an asbestos-containing material behind or within it. **In-scope site** a site, now Riverside House, Moorland View and Oakfield Lodge, with a confirmed asbestos register under this procedure.

Roles and responsibilities

**Facilities** maintains the asbestos register for each in-scope site, now including Oakfield Lodge, and makes it available for consultation before any relevant work. **Any staff member or contractor** planning work that disturbs a fabric surface checks the register first via facilities. **The registered manager** at an in-scope site, including Oakfield Lodge's registered manager for the first time, ensures staff are aware the register exists and how to consult it.

On-Call Manager Procedure

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how staff contact an on-call manager outside of normal hours for a care-related concern requiring senior management input. It applies to every site.

Policy statement

Out of hours, staff call their own region's on-call mobile number (North West, Midlands or South West) — the previous single central number has been decommissioned — providing a reliable route to senior management support with a manager who knows the calling region well.

Missing Person Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 July 2024. Immediate-search window shortened from 30 to 15 minutes.

1. Immediate search

A 15-minute site and immediate-grounds search is conducted (shortened from the previous 30 minutes)
before escalating further.

2. Police contact

If not found after the immediate search, police are called on 101 (or 999 if there is immediate risk).

Immediate response

Staff confirm the person is not elsewhere on site, note the last verified sighting, clothing, mobility,
communication needs and likely destinations, and preserve relevant CCTV or access records. The
registered manager assesses immediate vulnerability and calls emergency services without delay where
risk is high; local searching never postpones a necessary police report.

Search and communication

The search is coordinated, logged and allocated so unsafe duplication and unsearched areas are visible.
Staff maintain safe staffing for residents who remain on site. Family, commissioners and safeguarding
contacts are informed according to the person's plan and the circumstances, while public communication
and photographs are released only through the police-led or otherwise authorised route.

Return and learning

On return, immediate welfare and medical needs are assessed before a calm account is sought. The care
plan, risk assessment and known triggers are reviewed with the person and relevant representatives. The
incident record includes timings, decisions, notifications and search activity, and repeated episodes or
control failures are escalated for safeguarding and service-level review.

Frequently asked questions

**Should the medication fridge be opened to check on medication during a short outage?** No, keeping it closed preserves its temperature for several hours; it is only checked once power is confirmed restored, or if the outage becomes prolonged. **Who decides when to call the emergency generator supplier, where a site has one?** The on-call registered manager, once the 30-minute threshold is reached.

Key Cutting and Access Card Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 March 2025. Adds a new access-card return clause on leaving; removes the prior 4-week waiting period.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how a site key or access card is issued to, and returned by, a staff member. It applies to every permanent member of staff.

Policy statement

Site keys or access cards are issued to permanent staff from their first day, the previous 4-week waiting period having been removed, logged in the key register, and every key and access card must now be returned on an employee's last working day.

Definitions

**Key register** the log recording every key or access card issued, to whom, and when, and now its confirmed return date. **First-day issue** the new standard replacing the previous 4-week qualifying period. **Leaver return** the new requirement that every key and access card is returned before final pay is released.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager** authorises a key or access card issue from a staff member's first day, and confirms return on their last working day before final pay is released. **Facilities** cuts a key or programs an access card and updates the key register, now including the return date. **The staff member** keeps their key or access card secure, reports a lost one immediately, and returns it on their last working day.

Fire Evacuation Procedure — Riverside House

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how staff at Riverside House respond to a fire alarm and evacuate the building. It applies to every member of staff on shift, and is shared with every resident and visitor as appropriate to their understanding.

Policy statement

Riverside House uses a staged evacuation approach appropriate to a care setting where many residents have limited mobility, moving residents in immediate danger first while others are supported in a safe waiting area, rather than attempting a single simultaneous evacuation of the whole building.

Definitions

**PEEP** a Personal Emergency Evacuation Plan, prepared for every resident, setting out exactly how they are assisted to evacuate given their specific mobility and cognitive needs. **Fire warden** a trained staff member responsible for a specific zone during an evacuation. **Assembly point** the designated safe location outside the building where evacuated residents and staff gather.

Roles and responsibilities

**The fire warden on shift** directs the evacuation of their assigned zone according to each resident's PEEP. **The shift lead** calls the fire brigade, confirms the building is being evacuated, and accounts for every resident and staff member at the assembly point. **All staff** know the location of their nearest fire exit and evacuation equipment at all times.

On hearing the fire alarm, the fire warden for each zone begins evacuating residents according to their individual PEEP, prioritising anyone in immediate danger from the fire's location.

Call the fire brigade immediately; this is never delayed to first confirm whether the alarm is a false alert.

Use the evacuation chair for a resident whose PEEP requires it, only after staff have received evacuation chair training.

Move to the assembly point and complete a headcount against the day's resident and staff list, reporting any person unaccounted for to the fire brigade on arrival.

Asbestos Management Procedure

*Supersedes the version effective 1 January 2025. Oakfield Lodge added to scope following a newly confirmed asbestos survey; Harbour View, Meadow Court and Willow Bank remain out of scope as newer buildings.*

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group manages a confirmed asbestos register at a site where one applies. It now applies to Riverside House, Moorland View and Oakfield Lodge, following a newly confirmed asbestos survey at Oakfield Lodge; Harbour View, Meadow Court and Willow Bank remain out of scope as newer buildings.

Policy statement

Riverside House, Moorland View and now Oakfield Lodge each maintain an asbestos register; any work disturbing a fabric surface must check the register first, preventing accidental disturbance of a material that presents a serious health risk if damaged.

Definitions

**Asbestos register** the documented record of confirmed or presumed asbestos-containing material within a building, based on a professional survey. **Fabric surface** a wall, ceiling, floor or other building surface that may conceal an asbestos-containing material behind or within it. **In-scope site** a site, now Riverside House, Moorland View and Oakfield Lodge, with a confirmed asbestos register under this procedure.

Roles and responsibilities

**Facilities** maintains the asbestos register for each in-scope site, now including Oakfield Lodge, and makes it available for consultation before any relevant work. **Any staff member or contractor** planning work that disturbs a fabric surface checks the register first via facilities. **The registered manager** at an in-scope site, including Oakfield Lodge's registered manager for the first time, ensures staff are aware the register exists and how to consult it.

Purpose and scope

A complaint alleging abuse, or involving a serious injury, bypasses the normal complaints timescale entirely and is escalated to the Quality Lead within 4 hours, reflecting the urgency this category of complaint genuinely warrants.

Key Cutting and Access Card Procedure

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how a site key or access card is issued to a staff member. It applies to every permanent member of staff.

Policy statement

Site keys are issued only to permanent staff after 4 weeks' service, logged in the key register, reflecting a period of initial trust-building before a new staff member holds independent site access.

Definitions

**Key register** the log recording every key or access card issued, to whom, and when. **Qualifying period** the 4 weeks' service a permanent staff member must complete before a key or access card is issued. **Access card** the electronic alternative to a physical key used at a site with card-based access control.

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager** authorises a key or access card issue once the qualifying period is met. **Facilities** cuts a key or programs an access card and updates the key register. **The staff member** keeps their key or access card secure and reports a lost one immediately.

Confirm a staff member has completed 4 weeks' service before authorising a key or access card issue.

Log every key or access card issued in the key register, including the recipient and issue date.

Report a lost key or access card to Facilities immediately, who assesses whether a lock or access code change is needed.

Never share a personal key or access card with a colleague, even temporarily.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a genuine operational need requires earlier access (for example, a new senior staff member starting with immediate site responsibility), the registered manager may authorise an earlier issue with the reason documented, rather than the 4-week period applying rigidly regardless of role or circumstance.

Local and regional variations

A site using an access card system rather than physical keys, such as a more recently refurbished site, follows the same qualifying period and register logging, adapted to the electronic system's own audit trail.

Staff Handover Procedure

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out what a shift handover at Alderbridge Care Group must cover. It applies to every shift change at every site.

Policy statement

Each shift handover must cover any change in a person's condition, any incident during the shift, any outstanding task, and any visitor or professional attending, ensuring the incoming shift has a complete, accurate picture from the outset.

Definitions

**Shift handover** the structured exchange of information between an outgoing and incoming shift, covering every resident. **Outstanding task** a task identified but not completed during the outgoing shift, needing follow-up. **Change in condition** any observed change in a resident's physical or mental state during the shift.

Roles and responsibilities

**The outgoing shift lead** ensures every required element is covered in the handover, for every resident. **The incoming shift lead** confirms they have understood the handover and raises a question about anything unclear before the outgoing shift leaves. **Care staff** contribute a specific observation to the shift lead ahead of the formal handover.

Cover any change in a resident's condition observed during the outgoing shift, however minor it might seem.

Cover any incident that occurred during the shift, including one already recorded formally elsewhere, so the incoming shift has immediate awareness.

Cover any outstanding task, clearly stating what remains to be done and by when.

Cover any visitor or professional who attended during the shift, including the reason for their visit where relevant.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a handover must be unusually brief due to a genuine emergency requiring the outgoing shift's immediate attention elsewhere, the four required elements are still covered, even if more concisely than usual, rather than any element being skipped entirely.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This procedure works alongside the Incident Reporting Policy (the formal record a handover-mentioned incident also requires) and the Falls Prevention Policy (a fall during the shift is both a handover item and an incident record).

Incident Reporting Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how every accident, incident, near miss, medication error and property damage event
is reported, investigated and learned from at Alderbridge Care Group. It applies to every site and every
person present — staff, people supported, visitors and contractors.

Policy statement

Alderbridge treats thorough incident reporting as one of its most important safety tools, and actively
encourages reporting even where an event seems minor, since a genuine safety culture depends on
seeing the full picture, not only the events serious enough to be impossible to overlook.

Definitions

**Incident** any unplanned event that caused or could have caused harm or damage. **Near miss** an
event that could have caused harm but did not, on this occasion. **RIDDOR-reportable incident** an
incident meeting the specific statutory threshold requiring notification to the Health and Safety Executive.
**Root cause** the underlying, systemic reason an incident occurred, as distinct from its immediate,
surface-level cause.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any member of staff** witnessing or discovering an incident reports it the same shift using the
appropriate form. **The registered manager** reviews every incident at their site, escalating a
RIDDOR-reportable or otherwise serious incident to the Health and Safety Lead immediately. **The Health
and Safety Lead** coordinates cross-site trend analysis and reports to the quarterly Health and Safety
Committee.

1. Report every accident, incident and near miss using the appropriate form (the Accident and Incident
Report Form, Safeguarding Referral Form, or Medication Error Report Form as applicable) within 24
hours, regardless of how minor it seems.

2. Take any immediate action needed to make the situation safe before completing the paperwork, since
first aid and safety always come before documentation.

3. The registered manager reviews every report the same or next working day, identifying whether any
immediate further action is needed.

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group assesses falls risk and responds when a resident falls. It applies to every resident, with particular attention to a resident identified as being at higher risk.

Policy statement

Falls prevention balances a resident's right to move around freely with a proportionate response to their individual risk, since an overly restrictive approach can itself cause harm by reducing a resident's mobility, confidence and independence.

Definitions

**Falls risk assessment** the structured assessment completed for every resident at admission and reviewed regularly thereafter. **Post-fall protocol** the immediate response steps followed after any fall, regardless of apparent severity. **On-call registered manager** the manager reachable out of hours, who is the escalation contact for a fall under this version.

Roles and responsibilities

**Care staff** follow the post-fall protocol immediately after any fall and contact the on-call registered manager. **The registered manager** reviews the falls risk assessment after any fall and updates the care plan accordingly. **The GP or emergency services** are contacted where the post-fall protocol indicates a possible injury requiring clinical assessment.

Complete a falls risk assessment at admission and review it at least every three months, or sooner following any fall.

Following any fall, do not move the resident until a basic check for obvious injury has been completed, unless leaving them in place presents its own risk.

Contact the on-call registered manager immediately after any fall, regardless of whether an injury is apparent.

Call emergency services immediately for a suspected serious injury, such as a suspected fracture or head injury with loss of consciousness.

Record every fall, including one without apparent injury, in the resident's care record and the site's falls log.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a resident falls in a public area of the site with other residents present, staff prioritise the fallen resident's safety and dignity first, managing the immediate area calmly rather than treating other residents' reactions as the first concern.

Night Staff Procedure

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out the waking check standard for night staff at Alderbridge Care Group. It applies to every site running an overnight shift.

Policy statement

Night staff carry out a waking check of every resident at least once every 2 hours, or more frequently where the care plan specifies, balancing a resident's need for undisturbed sleep with the safety benefit of a regular check.

Definitions

**Waking check** a check where the staff member confirms the resident's wellbeing sufficiently to be satisfied they are safe, without necessarily fully waking a sleeping resident unnecessarily. **Individual care plan interval** a shorter interval than the standard 2 hours, specified for a resident whose needs require more frequent checking.

Roles and responsibilities

**Night staff** complete a waking check for every resident at least every 2 hours, recording each check. **The registered nurse or senior carer** sets an individual care plan interval for a resident whose needs require more frequent checking. **The registered manager** reviews waking check records as part of routine night-shift oversight.

1. Complete a waking check of every resident at least once every 2 hours through the night.
2. Follow a shorter, individually specified interval where a resident's care plan requires more frequent checking.
3. Record each waking check at the time it is completed, not retrospectively at the end of the shift.
4. Escalate immediately to the registered nurse or on-call manager if a waking check reveals a concern.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a resident is receiving end of life care and their care plan specifies a different, individually agreed checking approach, this takes precedence over the standard 2-hour interval, reflecting the different priorities appropriate to that stage of care.

Appendix: the five steps at a glance

For quick reference: identify hazards; identify who might be harmed; evaluate existing controls and residual risk; identify further action needed; record, communicate and review.

Assessing risk for a person with fluctuating needs

Where a person's needs fluctuate significantly (for example, a condition with good and bad days), the risk assessment records the range of presentation rather than a single snapshot, and staff are trained to recognise which end of that range they are seeing on a given day so the correct control measure is applied at the right time rather than a single fixed approach being used regardless of how the person actually presents that day.

Risk assessment for one-off events and visits

A one-off event (a fundraising open day, an external visit) receives its own proportionate risk assessment covering the event's specific hazards, completed with enough lead time to put any necessary control in place, rather than being run under a standing, unrelated risk assessment that does not actually address what is different about the event.

When a risk assessment reveals a risk that cannot be adequately controlled

Where an assessment finds a risk that cannot be reduced to an acceptable level with any available control, the activity does not proceed in that form; the registered manager and, where relevant, the Health and Safety Lead consider whether the activity can be modified to remove the unacceptable element, or whether it should not proceed at all, rather than proceeding regardless because stopping the activity feels operationally inconvenient.

Appendix: the two-stage test explained

This appendix explains the Act's own two-stage test in more practical detail. Stage one asks whether the person has an impairment or disturbance of the mind or brain, whether permanent or temporary — this alone does not determine incapacity, only whether the second stage needs to be considered at all. Stage two asks whether that impairment means the person cannot, at the time the decision needs to be made, understand relevant information about the decision, retain that information long enough to use it, weigh it up as part of the decision-making process, or communicate their decision by any means. A person lacks capacity for the specific decision only if stage one applies and they fail any one part of stage two — both stages genuinely matter, and staff are trained not to skip from 'has a diagnosis' straight to 'lacks capacity' without properly working through stage two.

Working with family members who hold Lasting Power of Attorney

Where a family member holds a registered Lasting Power of Attorney for health and welfare, or for property and financial affairs, staff confirm the specific scope of that authority before relying on it, since an attorney's authority is decision-specific to the type of LPA registered and does not automatically extend to every decision about the person, and Alderbridge keeps a copy of the registered document on file rather than relying on the family member's own description of their authority.

When a decision genuinely cannot wait

For a decision that must be made urgently and there is no attorney or existing best interests decision in place, the treating professional or care team makes the decision in the person's best interests using the information available at that moment, records the reasoning fully as soon as practicable afterward, and reviews it with fuller information once the urgency has passed, since acting reasonably with incomplete information in a genuine emergency is preferable to delaying necessary care while a more complete process is followed.

Missing Person Procedure

1. Immediate search

A 30-minute site and immediate-grounds search is conducted before escalating further.

2. Police contact

If not found after the immediate search, police are called on 101 (or 999 if there is immediate risk).

Immediate response

Staff confirm the person is not elsewhere on site, note the last verified sighting, clothing, mobility,
communication needs and likely destinations, and preserve relevant CCTV or access records. The
registered manager assesses immediate vulnerability and calls emergency services without delay where
risk is high; local searching never postpones a necessary police report.

Search and communication

The search is coordinated, logged and allocated so unsafe duplication and unsearched areas are visible.
Staff maintain safe staffing for residents who remain on site. Family, commissioners and safeguarding
contacts are informed according to the person's plan and the circumstances, while public communication
and photographs are released only through the police-led or otherwise authorised route.

Return and learning

On return, immediate welfare and medical needs are assessed before a calm account is sought. The care
plan, risk assessment and known triggers are reviewed with the person and relevant representatives. The
incident record includes timings, decisions, notifications and search activity, and repeated episodes or
control failures are escalated for safeguarding and service-level review.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how a key holder is nominated and contacted outside of normal hours at a North
West Region site. It applies to North West Region sites only, piloting the arrangement before any wider
rollout.

Policy statement

Each North West Region site nominates 2 key holders who may be called by the alarm monitoring
company outside of hours, providing a reliable way of responding to an out-of-hours alarm activation
without every incident requiring the registered manager personally.

Definitions

**Key holder** a nominated staff member who can attend site out of hours if the alarm monitoring company
calls. **Alarm monitoring company** the external company monitoring the site's alarm system and calling a

Roles and responsibilities

**The registered manager** nominates 2 key holders for their site and keeps the alarm monitoring
company's contact list current. **A nominated key holder** attends site promptly if called, assessing the
alarm activation and taking appropriate action. **Facilities** reviews the pilot's outcomes to inform a
decision on wider rollout.

1. Nominate 2 key holders per North West Region site, both confirmed by the registered manager and
registered with the alarm monitoring company.

2. Attend site within the timeframe agreed with the alarm monitoring company if called following an alarm
activation.

3. Assess the cause of the activation on arrival, resetting the alarm if it is a false activation or escalating
appropriately if a genuine concern is found.

4. Report every call-out to the registered manager the same day, including the cause and any action
taken.

Selecting a suitable key holder

A key holder is chosen for their proximity to the site and their ability to attend promptly, alongside their
seniority and familiarity with the site, since a key holder who lives some distance away undermines the
arrangement's whole purpose regardless of how experienced they otherwise are.

Replacing a key holder who leaves

Where a nominated key holder leaves Alderbridge or moves away from the site's local area, the registered
manager nominates a replacement promptly and updates the alarm monitoring company's contact list
immediately, rather than allowing the site to fall below its required 2 key holders even temporarily.

Closing note

A reliable key holder arrangement means an out-of-hours alarm activation is handled promptly without
every incident needing the registered manager personally, and this pilot exists to test that arrangement
properly before any wider rollout.

treatment beyond first aid.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a genuinely urgent situation means the post-referral review's 10-working-day window is not yet due
but a concern arises that the referral has stalled, the review is brought forward immediately rather than
waiting for the scheduled point.

Local and regional variations

Each local authority area has its own specific referral form, threshold guidance and contact structure, and
the regional manager for that area now supports the registered manager in navigating this where a
concern is genuinely complex.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This protocol sits alongside the Safeguarding Policy (Overarching), and now also references the On-Call
Manager Procedure's regional structure for the new regional manager liaison role.

Information sharing principles

Information is shared with an external agency on a need-to-know, proportionate basis, following the same
principle set out in the Safeguarding Policy (Overarching)'s own appendix.
